column3: (Content Security Policy (CSP) Header Not Set) — GitHub Pages can't send a real CSP header; a <meta> CSP was tried but ZAP flags meta-only frame-ancestors as invalid and it triggered a browser console error that failed the Lighthouse best-practices audit, so it was reverted.

(Missing Anti-clickjacking Header) — site is a static GitHub Pages deployment with no server to set X-Frame-Options; frame-ancestors CSP requires a real HTTP header (ignored via <meta>) which GH Pages can't send.
(X-Content-Type-Options Header Missing) — GitHub Pages serves static files without custom response headers; there is no server layer to add this header from.
(Information Disclosure - Suspicious Comments) — heuristic match on "TODO" markers in index.html; these are dev placeholders, not sensitive data.
(Storable/Cacheable Content) — static assets are deliberately cached by the CDN/browser; index.html is intentionally no-cache so deploys are picked up promptly.
(Permissions Policy Header Not Set) — GitHub Pages serves static files without custom response headers; there is no server layer to add this header from.
(Base64 Disclosure) — heuristic match on base64-looking strings in the built JS bundle; false-positive prone, not an actual secret leak.
(Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy Header Missing or Invalid) — GitHub Pages serves static files without custom response headers; there is no server layer to add this header from.
(Sec-Fetch-Dest Header is Missing) — this is a request header the browser sends; not something a static host can set.
